## Judged

- **judged-multi-spike-smell-ideation** [accepted-deviation]: ac-5's multi-claim smell is computed solely from declared spike stubs (BoardProjection.OQClaims tallies fm.Stubs only, projection.go), so the 'claimed by N spikes' observation renders only after graduation. DC-5's stated rationale for typing proto-stickies is to render the multi-spike-on-one-question smell live during ideation — 'the only moment it is actionable' — but two spike stickies whose yarn claims the same open question show no smell on the wall; the observation appears only once both have graduated into stubs. The implementation resolved the co-2 (frontmatter-only computation) vs DC-5 (live-during-ideation) tension entirely toward co-2, leaving the smell invisible at the moment the spec says it matters. (confidence 0.50) — Reaffirmed standing ruling at this re-judge: the frozen spec's own dc-5/co-2 tension, resolved toward the stricter constraint — sticky yarn is annotation-stream scratch, not the declared frontmatter co-2 closes computation over; the smell renders at graduation, where the claim becomes a declaration. The named follow-up stands: a ratified co-2 clarification if the owner wants dc-5's ideation-time render.
- **judged-feature-downward-blindness-static** [accepted-deviation]: ac-7 carries [static] evidence, but downward-blindness holds only by construction of the board paths, not by any static check: validateFeature (artifact/spec.go) never inspects fm.Links, and no VL rule refuses a feature document that hand-declares downward edges (e.g. an implements or depends-on link to its own story specs). Coverage-as-computed is structurally enforced (no declarable coverage field survives strict decode), but 'only stubs enter it' is unenforced against a hand-edited feature frontmatter carrying downward links — lint would pass such a document today. (confidence 0.35) — Accepted as a named lint follow-up rather than closed here: ac-7's coverage-is-computed half IS structurally enforced (no declarable coverage field survives strict decode — the bound static evidence), and the board's own write paths cannot mint downward edges; the unenforced residue is a hand-edited feature frontmatter declaring downward links, which lint passes today. The mechanical guard is a new VL rule (refuse feature-class specs carrying implements/depends-on edges to their own stories), and new lint vocabulary requires its ratified rule-table row — the designed path, not a closure-pass edit. Recorded as exactly the seam-detectors class the lifecycle-hygiene wall already parks; reversible the day that rule lands.
- **judged-stub-position-computed-only** [accepted-deviation]: The frozen spec's dc-6 declares 'stub cards take computed-only positions the way reference cards do... stored positions are deferred until dragging stubs proves needed', but the implementation stores dragged stub positions under 'stub:<slug>' layout keys (stubPositionKeyRe in artifact/boardlayout.go, VL-018 extended to admit them, citing a round 5.5 dc-6 amendment). The behavior is the decision's own anticipated reversal, but the spec text was never updated, so spec/scoping-canvas as written contradicts the shipped position model. (confidence 0.30) — Reaffirmed standing ruling at this re-judge: spec-text-vs-ratified-amendment errata, the R4-I-83 designed case — dc-6's computed-only clause carried its own reversal condition, round 5.5 ratified exactly that reversal (08-revision-notes, VL-018 extended, mirrors synced), and the identical tension was adjudicated no-conflict at spec/stub-cards' design-time sweep. The ratification record and this disposition are the correction's designed carriers.
